scope: Independent valid public DO identity/addressing and successful ordinary input admission. No native routing or guarded-core wave is reproduced or resumed.

cases.title: Readdress one named object through valid public helpers
trace: Mint the same name twice and parse its authentic serialized ID.
Write through get(idFromName), read through getByName and get(idFromString).
Write through the parsed address and read again through the original handle.
cases.oracle: The three valid helper routes reach exactly the same object and KV value in both write directions; client parsed ID omits the optional name. Server-side name retention after mixed addressing is not asserted.
cases.distinct: Existing identity coverage addresses class/script/binding separation and facet display identity. It never directly asserts valid namespace idFromString readdressing of durable state. No separate credit is assigned to same-name equality or getByName alone.
fixed_assertions: c.eq([named.equals(again),named.equals(parsed),parsed.equals(named)],[true,true,true],'valid named and parsed IDs compare equal');
c.eq([named.name,parsed.name],[name,undefined],'parsed address omits optional client name metadata');
c.eq([direct.id.toString(),shortcut.id.toString(),reopened.id.toString()],[named.toString(),named.toString(),named.toString()],'three public helper paths identify one object');
c.eq([first.value,second.value,third.value],['named-route','named-route','named-route'],'getByName and valid idFromString observe the named write');
c.eq((await c.send(direct,'read')).value,'parsed-route','write through parsed handle returns to original named address');

cases.title: Reopen isolated unique IDs from serialized addresses
trace: Mint two valid IDs using newUniqueId with default options.
Write only the first, establish the second is empty, then write the second.
Parse both serialized IDs and read their exact independent nameless object states.
cases.oracle: Both valid unique IDs reopen their own exact values and native object IDs; neither object receives the other value and no name metadata is invented.
cases.distinct: Exercises actual newUniqueId address creation and later valid string reopening, rather than a named ID, a supplied facet display ID or a changed namespace. Two samples are a finite identity check, not randomness/entropy/statistical collision certification.
fixed_assertions: c.eq(a.equals(b),false,'two ordinary random IDs name distinct fixture objects');
c.eq([a.name,b.name,left.name,right.name],[undefined,undefined,undefined,undefined],'unique IDs and their stubs have no name metadata');
c.eq((await c.send(rightParsed,'read')).value,null,'fresh independent random address has no left state');
c.eq(values.map(x=>[x.value,x.name]),[['unique-left',null],['unique-right',null]],'serialized unique addresses recover their own nameless states');
c.eq(values.map(x=>x.objectId),[a.toString(),b.toString()],'reopened unique objects report exact minted IDs');

cases.title: Preserve full routing past the name metadata boundary
trace: Create one 1024-byte Unicode name and two 1025-byte names differing only after the first 1024 bytes.
Write a distinct constant to each real object.
Readdress all three by their complete name and inspect recipient ID, optional name and stored value.
cases.oracle: Server ctx.id.name is retained through 1024 UTF-8 bytes and omitted for longer names; full names still route independently. Client stub.name retains each complete supplied name, including above that server metadata threshold.
cases.distinct: One compound byte-boundary/full-name contract. Cases are not split by length, suffix or Unicode parameter values. No malformed names, truncated IDs or cryptographic validation failures are submitted.
fixed_assertions: c.eq(names.map(n=>new TextEncoder().encode(n).length),[1024,1025,1025],'one exact UTF-8 metadata boundary with two distinct full-name suffixes');
c.eq([ids[0].equals(ids[1]),ids[1].equals(ids[2])],[false,false],'suppressed display metadata never truncates the routing name');
c.eq(rows.map(x=>x.name),[boundary,null,null],'object name metadata follows the byte boundary rather than JavaScript character count');
c.eq(rows.map(x=>x.value),['boundary','suffix-a','suffix-b'],'both long names readdress independent state using their entire name');
c.eq(rows.map(x=>x.objectId),ids.map(String),'all readdressed objects report exact original IDs');
c.eq(stubs.map(s=>s.name),names,'client stub retains the complete supplied name despite server metadata cutoff');

cases.title: Admit first requests after successful constructor initialization
trace: Start the first fetch to a fresh InitTarget whose constructor calls blockConcurrencyWhile.
Observe its hold through a separately addressed real Control DO.
Submit the second target fetch and complete an independent Record root write while the constructor remains held.
Witness held/unadmitted state, explicitly release Control, and join both target fetches.
cases.oracle: Both actual target handlers enter only after successful initialization and explicit release, and return initialized state. A separate root completes before release. Fallback expiration is BLOCKED, never positive evidence.
cases.distinct: Constructor readiness gates the very first event plus a newly arriving event. This is ordinary public initialization, with no nested blocks, competing gate owners, stale continuations, reset, timer failure, runtime fault or native-state seam.
fixed_assertions: c.eq(held.targetId,target.id.toString(),'constructor hold belongs to the requested live target');
c.eq((await c.send(peer,'write',{value:'peer-before-release'})).value,'peer-before-release','an independent ordinary root completes while constructor admission is closed');
c.eq([before.phase,before.entries.length,first.settled,second.settled],['held',0,false,false],'both incoming reads remain unadmitted at the witnessed constructor hold');
c.eq(results.map(x=>[x.value,x.ready,x.explicitRelease]),[['initialized',true,true],['initialized',true,true]],'first and queued requests see the fully completed successful initialization');
c.eq(after.entries.map(x=>x.request).sort(),['first','second'],'two distinct request handlers actually entered');
c.eq(after.entries.every(x=>x.afterRelease&&x.ready&&x.targetId===target.id.toString()),true,'every target admission follows explicit release and completed initialization');
c.eq(after.fallbackUsed,false,'no fallback timer supplied constructor completion');

cases.title: Gate one live root while its same-class peer progresses
trace: Seed an EventTarget before the gated request.
Start one ordinary request whose successful block writes intermediate state then awaits Control.
After the held witness, send a new read to that root and seed a second root of the same EventTarget class.
Witness peer completion while the target read is unadmitted; explicitly release, join writer/read and inspect the actual entry log.
cases.oracle: The same-class peer completes before release, the held target admits no reader, and the reader enters after explicit release with committed terminal state. No intermediate value can satisfy the fixed oracle.
cases.distinct: This is an already-live object and ordinary per-request block rather than constructor readiness or storage.transaction. The second same-class root directly distinguishes root-local admission from class-global blocking. No native gate contention, reentry or failure scenario is recreated.
fixed_assertions: c.eq((await c.send(target,'seed')).value,'seed','ordinary target is initialized before the request gate');
c.eq(held.targetId,target.id.toString(),'request hold belongs to the already live target');
c.eq((await c.send(peer,'seed')).value,'seed','a second root of the same class remains serviceable during the live request block');
c.eq([before.phase,before.entries.length,writer.settled,reader.settled],['held',0,false,false],'reader does not enter while the successful critical section awaits control');
c.eq(results.map(x=>[x.value,x.explicitRelease]),[['committed',true],['committed',true]],'reader observes the terminal write after ordinary gate release');
c.eq(after.entries.map(x=>[x.request,x.afterRelease,x.ready,x.targetId]),[['reader',true,true,target.id.toString()]],'actual reader admission is recorded after release with terminal local state');
c.eq(after.fallbackUsed,false,'no fallback timer supplied request completion');
